narrative.text: The cover of the English November 2019 WHO policy brief recommending social network-based HIV testing for key populations as part of partner services.

Explains that WHO recommends voluntary testing for the sexual and drug-injecting partners of people with HIV, but that key populations often fear stigma and breaches of confidentiality when naming partners. It defines social network-based testing, summarises review findings on its benefits and safety, and states the new recommendation.

Lists promising social network-based testing models and the operational principles of confidentiality, voluntariness and differentiated service choice. It gives LINKAGES project examples from the Democratic Republic of the Congo, Haiti and Malawi showing high HIV-positive yields among tested contacts.

Recommends offering partner services to newly diagnosed key population members at diagnosis and periodically, and weighing limited-wave versus ongoing network approaches. It addresses client safety and the need for monitoring indicators and reviewing programmes when harms occur, and includes WHO contact and licence details.
